messages:
reza: FYI planning a 'thermal ebb' maintenance tonight across us-central1 and apac-south1. Rolling NIC micro-updates + staggered GPU soft-restarts. Window 01:30-03:00 UTC. Goal: reduce transient thermal throttles seen last week and clear packet drops on a subset of blades. Minimal customer-facing impact expected.

elaine: How many racks/pools are in scope? any dedicated pools affected?

reza: Scope: 3 racks in us-central1, 2 racks in apac-south1. No dedicated/reserved pools touched unless explicit customer opt-in. We'll only touch interruptible and burst pools.

maria: Cost note: if we run spot backfill beyond 40 instances we exceed nightly budget by ~$1.2k. Can we keep <30 spot replacements?

reza: Yes aim for <=30 ephemeral backfills. We'll prefer warm-spare hot nodes first.

kai: Can we pre-seed KV cache on neighbor nodes to avoid cold-cache penalties?

reza: Yes. Preheat command will run 15m before each rack cordon. Script: 

```
# preheat kv cache on selectors
preheat --selector rack:rc-14 --keys-file /ops/cache/seeds.txt --parallel 4
```

elaine: Rollback conditions? I'm worried about p99 spikes for realtime routes.

reza: Rollback triggers:
- 5m p99 tail latency > 350ms for critical real-time routes
- error-rate delta > 4% over baseline for gen APIs
- NIC drop rate per-host > 500/s for 2 consecutive minutes
If any trigger fires, we run immediate abort and manual backfill.

tom: Drain sequence suggestion: cordon -> live-migrate containers (grace 45s) -> NIC firmware restart -> restart inference workers -> smoke test -> uncordon. Prefer process restarts vs full host reboots.

reza: Agree. We'll avoid full host reboots unless GPU hangs persist.

kai: ops-bot create stub and tag dashboards with maintenance tag please. Also schedule canary on single small tenant.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1795 (tag: thermal-ebb). Dashboards annotated: https://console.redwood/internal/incidents/INC-2026-1795

maria: Canary plan: pick tenant t-concise-2 (low traffic). If canary passes two rounds, proceed. If not, abort.

reza: Canary criteria: 10m steady p95 within 10% of baseline and no errors. Maria will own canary.

elaine: Who's on rollback call if canary fails? I can jump in, Tom will be on-call, Kai for routing changes.

tom: I'll prepare a fast-backfill runbook: `provisioner scale --pool warm-spare --count 20 && balancer reroute --policy preserve-reserved` and test it now.

reza: Also we'll set temporary routing to reduce batch sizes and prefer hot-kv:

```
routing.override=1
routing.batch_max=6
routing.prefer_cache=true
```

kai: Noted. I'll also throttle background heavy-batch jobs during the window.

maria: Reminder: customer comms email scheduled 22:45 UTC. Jordan will post to status page if any visible degradation occurs.

ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: 30m before window start.

reza: Final signoffs: Elaine (SLO watch), Tom (backfill script), Kai (routing), Maria (canary + comms). Kickoff 01:30 UTC. Post here when canary completes.
